outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning in Language Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the problem of mathematical reasoning in large language models, provides historical context, and outlines the motivation behind DeepSeekMath. Students will understand why mathematical reasoning is challenging for LLMs and what gaps exist between open-source and closed-source models.
subtopics: The Challenge of Mathematical Reasoning for LLMs
Current State of the Art: GPT-4, Gemini, and Open-Source Models
The Gap Between Open and Closed-Source Mathematical LLMs
Overview of DeepSeekMath's Approach and Key Contributions
Benchmarks for Mathematical Reasoning: GSM8K, MATH, and Beyond

outline.description: This chapter provides a comprehensive guide on how to construct large-scale, high-quality mathematical training data from web sources. Students will learn the iterative pipeline for data collection, the fastText classification approach, and decontamination procedures.
subtopics: The Importance of Training Data Quality for Mathematical Reasoning
Overview of Existing Mathematical Corpora: MathPile, OpenWebMath, Proof-Pile-2
Iterative Data Collection Pipeline from Common Crawl
FastText Classifier Training for Mathematical Content Detection
Domain-Based Identification and Human Annotation
Data Decontamination: Removing Benchmark Leakage
Corpus Quality Validation and Multilingual Considerations

outline.description: This chapter covers the pre-training methodology for creating a strong mathematical base model. Students will learn about the training configuration, the role of code pre-training, data mixing strategies, and comprehensive evaluation methodologies.
subtopics: Model Architecture and Initialization from DeepSeek-Coder
Training Configuration: Optimizer, Learning Rate Schedule, and Batch Size
Data Distribution Strategy: Math Corpus, Code, Natural Language, and arXiv
Evaluation Methodology: Chain-of-Thought, Tool-Use, and Formal Mathematics
Benchmark Results: Comparison with Minerva 540B and Open-Source Models
The Role of Code Pre-Training in Mathematical Reasoning
Why arXiv Papers May Be Ineffective for Mathematical Reasoning

outline.description: This chapter explains how to transform a base model into an instruction-following mathematical assistant. Students will learn about different solution formats, data curation strategies, and evaluation of instruction-tuned models.
subtopics: Instruction-Tuning Data Formats: Chain-of-Thought, Program-of-Thought, and Tool-Integrated Reasoning
Curating English and Chinese Mathematical Datasets
Training Configuration for Supervised Fine-Tuning
Evaluation Settings: With and Without Tool Use
Performance Comparison with Open-Source and Closed-Source Models
Strengths and Limitations of the Instruction-Tuned Model

outline.description: This chapter provides an in-depth technical explanation of GRPO, the novel reinforcement learning algorithm introduced in the paper. Students will understand the theoretical foundations, practical implementation, and advantages over PPO.
subtopics: Background: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for LLMs
Limitations of PPO: Memory Burden and Value Function Challenges
GRPO Core Idea: Group-Based Baseline Estimation
Mathematical Formulation of the GRPO Objective
Outcome Supervision vs. Process Supervision with GRPO
Iterative Reinforcement Learning Framework
Algorithm Implementation Details and Hyperparameters

outline.chapter_title: Reinforcement Learning for Mathematical Reasoning: DeepSeekMath-RL
outline.description: This chapter presents the application of GRPO to create the final reinforcement learning model. Students will learn about training procedures, reward model construction, and the empirical effectiveness of RL for mathematical reasoning.
subtopics: From DeepSeekMath-Instruct to DeepSeekMath-RL
Reward Model Training and Data Construction
Training Configuration and Hyperparameter Settings
In-Domain vs. Out-of-Domain Generalization
Performance Analysis: GSM8K and MATH Results
Comparison with Other RL Methods and Models

outline.chapter_title: A Unified Paradigm for Training Methods
outline.description: This chapter provides a theoretical framework for understanding various training methods in a unified manner. Students will learn to see SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO through a common lens and understand the key factors that differentiate them.
subtopics: Gradient-Based Formulation of Training Methods
Three Key Components: Data Source, Reward Function, and Algorithm
Comparing Methods: SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO
Online vs. Offline Data Sampling
Rule-Based vs. Model-Based Reward Functions
Gradient Coefficient Analysis Across Methods
Why Online Methods Outperform Offline Methods

outline.description: This chapter investigates the mechanisms behind RL's effectiveness for mathematical reasoning. Students will understand the difference between enhancing fundamental capabilities and improving output robustness, and explore future research directions.
subtopics: Pass@K vs. Maj@K Analysis: What RL Actually Improves
The Misalignment Problem in SFT Models
Understanding Output Distribution Robustness
Limitations of Current RL Approaches
Future Directions for Data Source: Tree-Search and Advanced Sampling
Future Directions for Algorithms: Robustness to Noisy Rewards
Future Directions for Reward Functions: Generalization and Uncertainty

outline.description: This chapter summarizes the key findings of DeepSeekMath, discusses its limitations, and provides practical guidance for students and practitioners working on mathematical reasoning in LLMs.
subtopics: Summary of DeepSeekMath's Achievements and Contributions
Key Lessons: Web Data Value, Code Training Benefits, arXiv Ineffectiveness
Model Limitations: Geometry, Theorem Proving, and Few-Shot Learning
Practical Recommendations for Building Mathematical LLMs
Open Problems and Future Research Directions
Ethical Considerations and Responsible AI Development
